title: Ringed Substructure and a Gap at 1 au in the Nearest Protoplanetary Disk
question: Does the TW Hya disk show ringed substructure in 870 um continuum at ~1 AU resolution, and what could cause it?

what.value: Broken power-law dust surface density prescription used in model

evidence.quote: we employed a broken power-law dust surface density prescription (cite: hogerheijde16)

recipe.method: Calibrate each execution, combine new and archival visibilities, phase-only self-cal
Multi-scale multi-frequency CLEAN at 345.9 GHz; two weightings
key_parameters: robust 0 (24x18 mas) and robust 0.5 + taper (30 mas)

recipe.method: Deproject to polar coordinates, azimuthally average; fit ellipses to rings/gap to get inclination and PA; compare azimuthal profiles
RADMC-3D model following Andrews 2012 with broken power-law, inner dust belt, truncation at 2.4 AU; gives temperature profile

evidence.quote: unresolved ($<$0.5 AU in radius) $0.93\pm0.04$ mJy source
a major axis position angle of $155\pm12$$^\circ$
a bright ring that peaks at 2.4 AU
we find at least a 30% brightness reduction
the median fractional deviation is only 7%

not_stated_but_needed: Cell size, image size, and CLEAN mask
Details of azimuthal averaging and ellipse fits
RADMC-3D model parameters (masses, radii, opacities, gas-to-dust)
score_reason: Data public and key settings (robust, beam, CASA version) given, but many imaging and analysis details missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, a recoverable imaging recipe, and numeric ring radii and geometry results.
